Subject: DPA redlines and subprocessor list — KineticCloud request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked promising. Our legal team reviewed the DPA and returned a set of redlines (attached). Two items are blocking approval on our end:

1) Kestrel requires the right to approve subprocessors that will process PHI-derived inference requests. The customer wants KineticCloud (third-party GPU provider) added as an approved subprocessor.
2) Narrower data use language: they want an explicit prohibition on models being used to improve third-party services or for training outside of the contracted environment.

We understand Redwood has standard language but KineticCloud is a preferred vendor for certain regions. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- accept a named-subprocessor addition for KineticCloud and
- add a clause that limits downstream model training/use on Kestrel-derived prompts/outputs?

Attached: Kestrel_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf

We need to present a response to procurement by end of week. Please loop in Product and Security if this requires an exception.

Thanks,
Claudia Ramos

Karthik / Dev / Evelyn — forwarding Kestrel's DPA redlines. They want KineticCloud named as an approved subprocessor and a stricter ban on using Kestrel data for model training.

From a sales/CS perspective we can win this account if we can offer a named-subprocessor exception for the specific region (us-west) and commit to a contractual prohibition on using customer data for training models outside the customer's environment.

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines and subprocessor list — KineticCloud request

Marissa — thanks for the context. Quick product take:

- Named subprocessor exceptions: technically doable if we scope to a specific deployment topology (dedicated hosts or a dedicated cluster in us-west). We cannot guarantee the same for hosted multi-tenant unless we have a dedicated pool because of dynamic scheduling.

- Data use restriction (no training): we can agree to contractual language that disallows using Kestrel-derived prompts/outputs for model training outside their tenancy, provided we enforce the following controls:
  * Dedicated inference instances (no shared KV cache)
  * Customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key) for model inputs/outputs at rest
  * KV/prefix caching disabled for that customer
  * Retention policy: logs containing prompts/outputs truncated to 24 hours unless explicitly approved for longer retention for debug with customer consent

Operational impact: dedicating a cluster increases cost and reduces scheduling flexibility. We'll need to include a one-time onboarding fee and a modest monthly uplift. Dev, can you estimate the infra/ops delta?

Suggested contract language snippets for legal: (1) "Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve or train any models outside of the Customer's dedicated tenancy"; (2) "Redwood will list KineticCloud as an approved subprocessor for the Customer's Dedicated Cluster provisioned in the us-west region."

If Security is comfortable with the controls above, Product can sign off on an exception policy and we can surface the pricing uplift to the customer.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines and subprocessor list — KineticCloud request

Team — reviewed the proposed compensating controls. Security position: conditional approval with the following non-negotiables:

1) KineticCloud must provide a current SOC 2 Type II report and complete our subprocessor questionnaire. No exception without SOC 2 evidence.
2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) must be enforced for the dedicated cluster; Redwood must not hold plaintext customer data keys.
3) We require end-to-end encryption for inference payloads in transit and at rest; logs that include user prompts/outputs must be redacted or hashed before being stored longer than 24 hours.
4) No shared model training pipelines may access any storage or telemetry from the dedicated cluster. We need contractual language explicitly prohibiting use of Customer Data for model training and specifying audit rights (quarterly attestation + spot checks).

If Kestrel accepts the above, Security will sign off and Legal can finalize the DPA amendments. If Kestrel insists on multi-tenant hosted with no BYOK, we should decline — the residual risk is too high for PHI-adjacent workloads.

Dev — please provide an ops estimate for dedicated cluster provisioning, monthly run-rate delta, and an onboarding SLA (time to provision). I need these numbers to include in the exception memo.

Evelyn Hart
Director of Security & Compliance
